subject: Emotions
title: Empathy in Conflict
description: A micro-lesson that makes Empathy in Conflict usable.

hook.text: Two people argue. Each waits for their turn to rebut. Neither listens. The fight intensifies for hours.

buildup.text: Marshall Rosenberg's Nonviolent Communication teaches: during conflict, reflect the other person's feelings first.

discovery.text: When someone feels heard, their nervous system calms. Defensiveness drops. Only then can they hear your side.

twist.text: Empathy in conflict doesn't mean agreeing. It means saying 'I see you're frustrated' before saying 'Here's my view.'

climax.text: Studies show couples who validate each other's emotions before problem-solving resolve issues 40% faster.

punchline.text: First make them feel heard. Then ask to be heard.
